stocks and corporate bonds and interest rate swaps accounted under other financial assets.</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Recognition and measurement</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The purchase and sale of financial
assets are recognized at the date on which the Group commits to purchase or sale the asset.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.4pt 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Financial assets valued at amortized
cost are initially recognized at their fair value plus cost of transaction. These assets accrue interest according to the effective interest
rate method.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Financial assets valued at fair
value through profit or loss and other comprehensive income are initially recognized at fair value, and transaction costs are recognized
as expenses in the comprehensive income statement. Subsequently, they are valued at fair value. Changes in fair value and income from
the sale of financial assets at fair value through profit or loss and other comprehensive income are recorded in Finance Income or Finance
Expenses and Other comprehensive income, respectively, in the consolidated statement of income and comprehensive income, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">In general, the Group uses the transaction
price to determine the fair value of a financial instrument at the initial recognition. In the rest of the cases, the Group only records
gain or loss at initial recognition if the fair value of the instrument is evidenced with other comparable and visible transactions of
the market for the same instrument or if it is based on a valuation technique that only includes visible market data. Gains or loss not
recognized at the initial recognition of a financial asset is later recognized as long as they derive from a change in factors (including
time) in which the market participants consider establishing the price.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The profit or loss of debt instruments
which are measured at amortized cost and are not designated as hedge instruments are recognized in profit or loss when the financial assets
are derecognized or when impairment is recognized and during the amortization process by using the effective interest rate method. The
Group only reclassifies all investments in debt instruments when it changes the business model used to manage those assets.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Derecognition of financial assets</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A financial asset (or, where applicable,
a part of a financial asset or part of a group of similar financial assets) is derecognized; that is to say, it is deleted from the statement
of financial position, when:</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.35pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span style="font-size: 10pt">the contractual rights to receive cash flows from the asset have expired;</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: justify; padding-right: 20.15pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">the contractual rights to receive cash flows from
the asset have been transferred or an obligation has been assumed to pay the received cash flows in full without material delay to a third
party under a &#8216;pass-through&#8217; arrangement; and either (a) all the risks and rewards of the asset have been transferred substantially,
or</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.2pt 0 27.45pt; text-align: justify">(b) all the risks and rewards
of the asset have neither been transferred nor retained substantially, but control of the asset has been transferred.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">When the contractual rights to
receive cash flows from an asset have been transferred or a pass-through arrangement has been entered into, but all of the risks and rewards
of the asset have neither transferred nor retained substantially and no control of it has been transferred, such asset shall continue
to be recognized to the extent of the Group&#8217;s continuing involvement in it. In this case, the Group shall also recognize the associated
liability. The transferred asset and the associated liability are measured on a basis that reflects the rights and obligations that the
Group has retained.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Impairment of financial assets</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">IFRS 9 establishes an &#8220;expected
credit loss&#8221; model (&#8220;ECL&#8221;). This requires the application of considerable judgment with regard to how changes in economic
factors affect ECL, which is determined over a weighted average base. ECL results from the difference between contractual cash flows
and cash flows at current value that the Group expects to receive.</p>
<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"></p>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_233_zEXmVBByYQYh" style="font: bold 12pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 4.1pt 16.05pt 0 4.25pt; text-align: center">CENTRAL PUERTO S.A.</p></ix:exclude>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_232_zjGVQrzLEKb6" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_231_zc0exX7GvmY3" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The impairment model set forth by
IFRS 9 is applicable to the financial assets measured at amortized value or at fair value through changes in other comprehensive income,
except for the investment in equity securities and assets from the contracts recognized under IFRS 15.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Pursuant to IFRS 9, loss allowances
are measured using one of the following bases:</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.4pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left; padding-right: 20.2pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">The 12-month ECL: these are expected credit losses that
result from those default events on the financial instrument that are possible within 12 months after the reporting date; and</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left; padding-right: 20.2pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Full lifetime expected credit losses: these are expected
credit losses that result from all possible default events over the life of the financial instrument.</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Given the nature of the clients with
which the Group operates and on the base of the foregoing criteria, the Group did not identify expected credit losses.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 19.95pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">With regard to financial placements
and according to the placement policies in force, the Group monitors the credit rate and the credit risk of these instruments. Pursuant
to the analysis, the Group did not identify the need to record impairment of these types of instruments.</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.45pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 45pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.9.2.</span></td><td style="text-align: left">Financial liabilities</td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify"><b>Initial recognition and subsequent measurement</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Financial liabilities are classified,
at initial recognition, as financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss, loans and borrowings, accounts payables or as derivatives
designated as hedging instruments in an effective hedge ratio, as appropriate.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Financial liabilities are initially recognized
at their fair value, net of the incurred transaction costs. Since the Group has no financial liabilities whose characteristics require
the fair value accounting, according to IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), after
the initial recognition, the financial liabilities are valued at amortized cost. Any difference between the amount received as financing
(net of transaction costs) and the reimbursement value is recognized in comprehensive income throughout the life of the debt financial
instrument using the method of effective interest rate.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Regarding the loan with Mitsubishi Corporation,
described in Note 13.3.11., the initial recognition was at its fair value and subsequently the loan is measured at amortized cost. The
mentioned loan includes a scheme of annual repayments with minimum payments, which can increase according to the free cash flows of the
previous year of the controlled company Central Costanera S.A. If there are changes in the estimated free cash flows that result in changes
in future capital payments, the Group recognizes the impact within financial income or financial costs, as appropriate, in the comprehensive
income statement for the year in which such change in estimate occurs.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">At the closing date of these consolidated
financial statements, the financial liabilities classified as loans and borrowings and accounts payables of the Group include Trade and
other payables, and Loans and borrowings.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.65pt; text-align: justify">Derecognition of financial liabilities</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A financial liability is derecognized when
the obligation under the liability is discharged or cancelled or expires.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">When an existing financial liability
is replaced by another from the same lender on substantially different terms, or the terms of an existing liability are substantially
modified, such an exchange or modification is treated as a derecognition of the original liability and the recognition of a new liability,
and the difference in the respective carrying amounts is recognized as finance income or costs in the statement of income, as the case
may be.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_239_zh0y2awOfCoj" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_239_zVkRVHYxVMPf" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 45pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.9.3.</span></td><td style="text-align: left">Offsetting financial assets and financial liabilities</td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Financial assets and financial
liabilities are offset, and the net amount presented in the statement of financial position if, and only if, there is a currently enforceable
legal right to offset the recognized amounts and there is an intention to settle on a net basis, or to realize the assets and settle the
liabilities simultaneously.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 45pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.9.4.</span></td><td style="text-align: left">Financial assets and liabilities with related parties</td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Assets and liabilities with related
parties are recognized initially at fair value plus directly attributable transaction costs. As long as credits and debts with related
parties do not derive from arms-length transactions, any difference arising at the initial recognition between such fair value and the
consideration given or received in return shall be considered as an equity transaction (capital contribution or payment of dividends,
which will depend on whether it is positive or negative).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Following initial recognition,
these receivables and payables are measured at their amortized cost through the effective interest rate (EIR) method. The EIR amortization
is included in finance income or costs or other operating income or expenses in the statement of income, depending on the nature of the
liability giving rise to it.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 45pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.9.5.</span></td><td style="text-align: left">Derivative financial instruments and hedge accounting</td></tr></table>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 197.5pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0in">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt/200% Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 8.35pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0in">Initial recognition and subsequent measurement</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The derivative financial instruments
used by the Group are initially recognized through their fair values at the date on which the contract is entered into, and they are subsequently
measured again at their fair value. The derivative financial instruments are accounted as financial assets when their fair value is positive
and as financial liabilities when their fair value is negative.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The method to recognize the loss or
income from the change in fair value depends on whether the derivative was determined as a hedge instrument; in such case, on the nature
of the item it is covering. The Company can determine certain derivative as:</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.35pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Fair value hedge;</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Cash flow hedge;</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.35pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">At the beginning of the transaction,
the Group records the relationship between the hedge instruments and items covered, as well as its objectives for risk management and
the strategy to make different hedge operations. It also records its assessment, both at the beginning and on a continuous base, on whether
the derivatives used in the hedge transactions are highly effective to compensate changes in fair value or in the cash flows of the items
covered.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Fair value hedge</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Changes in fair value of derivatives
determined and classified as fair value hedge are recorded in the statement of comprehensive income together with any change in the fair
value of the covered asset or liability attributable to the covered risk.</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.5pt 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Cash flow hedge</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The effective part of changes
in fair value of the derivatives determined and classified as cash flow hedge are recognized in Other comprehensive income. The loss or
income related to the non-effective part is immediately recognized in the consolidated statement of income within the Finance Expenses
or Finance Income, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.5pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The cumulative amounts in Other
comprehensive income are recorded in the consolidated statement of income in the periods in which the item covered affects the consolidated
statement of income. In the case of interest rates hedge, this means the amounts recognized in equity are reclassified as net finance
income (loss) as interest is accrued on associated debts.</p>
<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.5pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"></p>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_23F_zkyBJmgRb5G6" style="font: bold 12pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 4.1pt 16.05pt 0 4.25pt; text-align: center">CENTRAL PUERTO S.A.</p></ix:exclude>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_230_zASHQMyaiyJc" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">As at December 31, 2024, the
Group has no hedging derivative instruments. Hence, swap contracts of interest rate are measured at their current value at the closing
of each period or fiscal year and are stated as assets or liabilities depending on the rights and obligations emerging from the respective
contracts. In this way, changes in the accounting measure of such contracts are recognized in the consolidated statement of income under
finance income or finance cost, as applicable.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001267" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForMeasuringInventories"><p id="xdx_84E_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForMeasuringInventories_zvIEy2ta7dol" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 36pt">2.2.10.</td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_864_z4ac68dfGo5j">Inventories</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.05pt">Inventories
are valued at the lower of restated acquisition cost and net realizable value. In the estimation of recoverable values, the purpose of
the asset to be measured and the movements of items of slow or scarce rotation are taken into account. Inventories balance is not higher
than its net realizable value at the corresponding dates.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001269" name="CEPU:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForCashAndCashEquivalentsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_845_ecustom--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForCashAndCashEquivalentsExplanatory_z1Q3iwgmTLQe" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.05pt">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 36pt">2.2.11.</td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_86D_z6lNtSPQ3Zj">Cash and cash equivalents</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Cash is deemed to include both
cash fund and freely-available bank deposits on demand. Short-term deposits are deemed to include short-term investments with significant
liquidity and free availability that, subject to no previous notice or material cost, may be easily converted into a specific cash amount
that is known with a high degree of certainty upon the acquisition, are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value, maturing
up to three months after the date of the related acquisitions, and whose main purpose is not investment or any other similar purpose,
but settling short-term commitments.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">For the purpose of the consolidated
statement of financial position and the consolidated statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents comprise cash at banks and on
hand and short-term investments meeting the abovementioned conditions.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001271" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForProvisionsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_846_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForProvisionsExplanatory_z5G10APq0F1l" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 36pt">2.2.12.</td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_86B_ztQDHLPWTtta">Provisions</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Provisions are recognized when
the Group has a present obligation (legal or constructive) as a result of a past event, it is probable that an outflow of resources embodying
economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation and a reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation. Where
the Group expects some or all of a provision to be reimbursed, for example under an insurance contract, the reimbursement is recognized
as a separate asset but only when the reimbursement is virtually certain. The expense relating to any provision is presented in the statement
of income under the item that better reflects the nature of the provision net of any reimbursement to the extent that the latter is virtually
certain.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 19.95pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">If the effect of the time value of
money is material, provisions are discounted using a current pre-tax market rate that reflects, where appropriate, the risks specific
to the liability. Where discounting is used, the increase in the provision due to the passage of time is recognized as a finance cost
in the consolidated statement of income.</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.35pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Provision for lawsuits and claims</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">In the ordinary course of business,
the Group is exposed to claims of different natures (e.g., commercial, labor, tax, social security, foreign exchange or customs claims)
and other contingent situations derived from the interpretation of current legislation, which result in a loss, the materialization of
which depends on whether one more events occur or not. In assessing these situations, Management uses its own judgment and advice of its
legal counsel, both internal and external, as well as the evidence available as of the related dates. If the assessment of the contingency
reveals the likelihood of the materialization of a loss and the amount can be reliably estimated, a provision for lawsuits and claims
is recorded as of the end of the reporting period.</p>

<p style="font: 11pt/200% Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 279.55pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 1.05pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 7pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
</span><span style="font-size: 10pt">Provision for wind and solar farms dismantling See Note 23.</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001275" name="CEPU:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForContingentLiabilitiesExplanatory"><p id="xdx_840_ecustom--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForContingentLiabilitiesExplanatory_zrJccrVlEjpg" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.13.</span></td><td style="text-align: justify"><span id="xdx_86D_zkb63DQPpVdk">Contingent liabilities</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A contingent liability is: (i)
a possible obligation that arises from past events and whose existence will be confirmed only by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one
or more uncertain future events not wholly within the control of the entity; or (ii) a present obligation that arises from past events
but is not recognized because:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 19.95pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">(a) it is not probable that an
outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation; or (2) the amount of the obligation cannot
be measured with sufficient reliability.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A contingent liability is not recognized
in financial statements; it is reported in notes, unless the possibility of an outflow of resources to settle such liability is remote.
For each type of contingent liability as of the relevant reporting period-end dates, the Group shall disclose (i) a brief description
of the nature of the obligation and, if possible, (ii) an estimate of its financial impact; (iii) an indication of the uncertainties about
the amount or timing of those outflows; and (iv) the possibility of obtaining potential reimbursements.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001277" name="CEPU:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForContingentAssetsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_842_ecustom--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForContingentAssetsExplanatory_zIdvrMAdO50f" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0.05pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.14.</span></td><td style="text-align: justify"><span id="xdx_866_z13YEZZSUedb">Contingent assets</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A contingent asset is a possible
asset that arises from past events and whose existence will be confirmed only by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain
future events not wholly within the control of the Group.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 19.95pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">A contingent asset is not recognized
in financial statements; it is reported in notes only where an inflow of economic benefits is probable. For each type of contingent asset
as of the relevant reporting period-end dates, the Group shall disclose (i) a brief description of the nature thereof and, if possible,
(ii) an estimate of its financial impact.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001279" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForEmployeeBenefitsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_845_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForEmployeeBenefitsExplanatory_zLF4FIRJVnC5" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.15.</span></td><td style="text-align: justify"><span id="xdx_862_zxenWMzkb2Vf">Employee benefits</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Employee short-term benefits:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group recognizes short-term benefits
to employees, such as salary, vacation pay, bonuses, among others, on an accrued basis and includes the benefits arising from collective
bargaining agreements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Post-employment employee long-term
benefits:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group grants benefits to all trade-union
employees when obtaining the ordinary retirement benefit under the Argentine Integrated Pension Fund System, based on multiples of the
relevant employees&#8217; salaries.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.3pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The amount recognized as a liability
for such benefits includes the present value of the liability at the end of the reporting period, and it is determined through actuarial
valuations using the projected unit credit method.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Actuarial gains and losses are fully
recognized in other comprehensive income in the period when they occur and immediately allocated to unappropriated retained earnings (accumulated
losses), and not reclassified to income in subsequent periods.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group recognizes the net
amount of the following amounts as expense or income in the statement of income for the reporting year: (a) the cost of service for the
current period; (b) the cost of interest; (c) the past service cost, and (d) the effect of any curtailment or settlement.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Other long-term employee benefits:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group grants seniority-based benefits
to all trade-union employees when reaching a specific seniority, based on their normal salaries.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The amount recognized as liabilities
for other long-term benefits to employees is the present value of the liability at the end of the reporting period. The Group recognizes
the net amount of the following amounts as expense or income: (a) the cost of service for the current period; (b) the cost of interest;
(c) actuarial income and loss, which shall be recognized immediately and in full; (d) the past service cost, which shall be recognized
immediately and in full; and (e) the effect of any curtailment or settlement.</p>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_230_zYUlAycYYFDa" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>
<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001283" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSharebasedPaymentTransactionsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_846_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSharebasedPaymentTransactionsExplanatory_zlQPQtDMaSF3" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.16.</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_867_z9VuCgRqeL1h">Share-based payments</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.3pt 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The cost of share-based payments
transactions that are settled with equity instruments is determined by the fair value at the date when the grant is made using an appropriate
valuation model.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.4pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">This cost is recognized in the
consolidated financial statements under employee benefits expense, together with a corresponding total increase in non-controlling interest.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">On January 18, 2017, the subsidiary
CP Renovables S.A. (&#8220;CPR&#8221;) entered into a stock option agreement with its minority shareholder at that time that was also
its chairman and general manager and a shareholder of the Company (the &#8220;minority shareholder&#8221;). Under such agreement the minority
shareholder had the right to purchase class B shares of CPR that represented 10% of the fully diluted capital stock of CPR. The option
was exercisable in whole or in part, at any time prior to the seventh anniversary of the date of the stock option agreement. On November
15, 2023, the minority shareholder exercised the option and acquired the shares representing 10% of the capital stock of CPR. See Consolidated
Statement of Changes in Equity. As of December 31, 2023 all assumed obligations under the stock option agreement were met.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001285" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForInvestmentInAssociates"><p id="xdx_84B_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForInvestmentInAssociates_z49GM35lnWDg" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.17.</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_861_zTY1x4ELnOaf">Investment in associates</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.3pt 20.05pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The Group&#8217;s investments
in associates are accounted for using the equity method. An associate is an entity over which the Group has significant influence. Significant
influence is the power to participate in the financial and operating policy decisions of the investee, but is neither control nor joint
control.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.25pt 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">According to the equity method,
investments in associates are originally booked in the statement of financial position at cost, plus (less) the changes in the Group&#8217;s
ownership interests in the associates&#8217; net assets subsequent to the acquisition date. If any, goodwill relating to the associate
is included in the carrying amount of the investment and is neither amortized nor individually tested for impairment.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.4pt 20.25pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">If the cost of the investments
is lower than the proportional share as of the date of acquisition on the fair value of the associate&#8217;s assets and liabilities,
a gain is recognized in the period in which the investment was acquired.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.4pt 20.2pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The statement of income reflects
the share of the results of operations of the associates adjusted on the basis of the fair values estimated as of the date on which the
investment was incorporated. When there has been a change recognized directly in the equity of the associates, the Group recognizes its
share of any changes and includes them, when applicable, in the statement of changes in equity.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.25pt 20.25pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The Group&#8217;s share of profit
of an associate is shown in a single line on the main body of the consolidated statement of income. This share of profit includes income
or loss after taxes of the associates.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.4pt 20.05pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The financial information of the
associates is prepared for the same reporting period as the Group. When necessary, adjustments are made to bring the accounting policies
of the associates in line with those of the Group.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.15pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">After application of the equity
method, the Group determines whether it is necessary to recognize impairment losses on its investment in its associates. At each reporting
date, the Group determines whether there is objective evidence that the value of investment in the associates has been impaired. If such
was the case, the Group calculates the amount of impairment as the difference between the recoverable amount of the investment in the
associates and its carrying value, and recognizes the loss as &#8220;Share of losses of an associate&#8221; in the consolidated statement
of income.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The information related to associates
is included in Note 3.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001290" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSegmentReportingExplanatory"><p id="xdx_84D_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSegmentReportingExplanatory_z4SJBsuxWPN1" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.18.</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_864_zhIQTvOsd0La">Information on operating segments</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.2pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">For management purposes, the Group
is organized in four different business units to carry out its activities, as follows:</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.4pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: justify; padding-right: 20.3pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Electric power generation from conventional sources:
the Group is engaged in the production of electric power from conventional sources and its sale.</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: justify; padding-right: 20.3pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Electric power generation from renewable sources:
the Group also is engaged in the production of electric power from renewable sources and its sale.</span></td></tr></table>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.4pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 9.45pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: justify; padding-right: 20.15pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Natural gas transport and distribution: through
its equity investees companies belonging to ECOGAS Group, the Group is engaged in the natural gas distribution public sector service in
the Cuyo and Centro regions of Argentina and it is also engaged in the natural gas transport sector service through its equity investee
Company Transportadora de Gas del Mercosur S.A. Also, the Company resells certain gas transport and distribution capacity that was previously
contracted by the Company.</span></td></tr></table>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: 11pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.45pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 18pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#8211;</span></td><td style="text-align: justify; padding-right: 20.1pt"><span style="font-size: 10pt">Forestry activity: the Group is engaged in the forestation,
reforestation, woods plantation and commercialization of its products.</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The financial performance of segments
is evaluated based on operating income / expense before depreciation, amortization and impairment ("Adjusted EBITDA") (Note
4). The group of executive directors is the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) and monitors the Adjusted EBITDA of its business units
separately for the purpose of making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001292" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForBiologicalAssetsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_841_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForBiologicalAssetsExplanatory_zecMVKlXT7Jj" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.19.</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_86D_zYwGVXY0XFq5">Biological assets</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 20pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Forestry plantations are measured,
both on initial recognition and at the end of the reporting period, at their fair value, less costs of sale at harvest or collection point.
Fair value of the plantations with no available market prices under their current condition is determined through discounted cash flows,
using market discount rates.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.3pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Forestry plantations included in the
harvest plan for the twelve months following the closing of the period are classified as current biological assets.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001294" name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForBusinessCombinationsExplanatory"><p id="xdx_846_eifrs-full--DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForBusinessCombinationsExplanatory_zOxC85OoXBu5" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left"></p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.45pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 35.05pt"><span style="letter-spacing: -0.05pt">2.2.20.</span></td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_865_zEPEOW4wjZcg">Business combinations</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Business combinations are accounted
for using the acquisition method when the Group takes effective control of the acquired company.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group will recognize in
its financial statements the acquired identifiable assets, the assumed liabilities, any non-controlling interest and, if any, goodwill
according to IFRS 3.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The acquisition cost is measured as
the aggregate of the transferred consideration, measured at fair value on that date, and the amount of any non-controlling interest in
the acquiree. The Group will measure the non- controlling interest in the acquiree at fair value or at the proportional interest in the
identifiable net assets of the acquiree.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">If the business combination is made
in stages, the Group will measure again its previous holding at fair value at the acquisition date and will recognize income or loss in
the consolidated statement of comprehensive income.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.5pt 19.95pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Goodwill is measured at cost,
as the excess of the transferred consideration regarding the acquired identifiable assets and the net assumed liabilities of the Group.
If this consideration is lower than the fair value of the identifiable assets and of the assumed liabilities, the difference is recognized
in the consolidated statement of income. If the fair value of the net assets acquired is higher than the consideration paid, the Group
reassesses whether it has properly identified all the assets acquired and all the liabilities assumed and reviews the procedures used
to measure the amounts to be recognized at the acquisition date. If the reassessment still results in an excess of the fair value of
the net assets acquired in comparison to the consideration paid, then the gain is recognized in the consolidated statement of income.</p>
<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.5pt 19.95pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"></p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.4pt"/><td style="width: 27pt">2.3.</td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_863_zv5KP1fkU4wf">Significant accounting estimates and assumptions</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The preparation of the Group&#8217;s
financial statements requires management to make significant estimates and assumptions that affect the recorded amounts of revenues, expenses,
assets and liabilities, and the disclosure of contingent liabilities, at the end of the reporting period. In this sense, the uncertainties
related to the estimates and assumptions adopted could give rise in the future to final results that could differ from those estimates
and require significant adjustments to the amounts of the assets and liabilities affected.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The key assumptions concerning the future
and other key sources of estimation uncertainty at the end of the reporting period, that have a significant risk of causing a material
adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within the next financial year, are described below. The Group based its
accounting assumptions and significant estimates on parameters available when the financial statements were prepared. Existing circumstances
and assumptions about future developments, however, may change due to market changes or circumstances arising beyond the control of the
Group. Such changes are reflected in the assumptions when they occur.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify"><i>Recoverability of property, plant
and equipment and intangible assets:</i></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 19.95pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">At each closing date of the reported
period, the Group evaluates if there is any sign that the property, plant and equipment and/or intangible assets with finite useful lives
may have their value impaired. Impairment exists when the book value of assets related to the Cash Generating Unit (CGU) exceeds its recoverable
value, which is the higher between its fair value less costs of sale of such asset and value in use. The value in use is calculated through
the estimation of future cash flows discounted at their present value through a discount rate that reflects the current assessments of
the market over the temporal value of money and the specific risks of each CGU. The recoverable value is sensitive to the estimated inflows
as well as the discount rate applied.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.4pt 19.95pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify"></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001309" name="CEPU:DescriptionForAccountingPolicyForChangesInAccountingPolicies"><p id="xdx_840_ecustom--DescriptionForAccountingPolicyForChangesInAccountingPolicies_z2IE3m4mV1W6" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 11.45pt; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 27pt">2.4.</td><td style="text-align: left"><span id="xdx_865_zAGeyBZjnRn4">Changes in accounting policies</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"><b>New standards and interpretations
adopted</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 22.45pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">As from the fiscal year beginning
January 1, 2024, the Group has applied for the first time certain new and/or amended standards and interpretations as issued by the IASB.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.25pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Below is a brief description
of the new and/or amended standards and interpretations adopted by the Group and their impact on these consolidated financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Amendments to IAS 1: Classification
of Liabilities as Current or Non-current</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">In January 2020 and October 2022,
the IASB issued amendments to paragraphs 69 to 76 of IAS 1 to specify the requirements for classifying liabilities as current or non-current.
The amendments clarify: (i) the meaning of a right to defer settlement; (ii) that a right to defer must exist at the end of the reporting
period; (iii) that classification is unaffected by the likelihood that an entity will exercise its deferral right and (iv) that only if
an embedded derivative in a convertible liability is itself an equity instrument would the terms of a liability not impact its classification.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">In addition, a requirement has
been introduced to disclose when a liability arising from a loan agreement is classified as non-current and the entity&#8217;s right to
defer settlement is contingent on compliance with future covenants within twelve months.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.25pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">These amendments have not had a significant
impact on the Group's financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.45pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Supplier Finance Arrangements
- Amendments to IAS 7 and IFRS 7</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.15pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">In May 2023, the IASB issued
amendments to IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows and IFRS 7 Financial Instruments: Disclosures to clarify the characteristics of supplier finance
arrangements and require additional disclosure of such arrangements. The disclosure requirements in the amendments are intended to assist
users of financial statements in understanding the effects of supplier finance arrangements on an entity&#8217;s liabilities, cash flows
and exposure to liquidity risk.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.3pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">These amendments have not had a significant
impact on the Group's financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Amendments to IFRS 16: Lease liability
in subsequent sale and leaseback</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 10.35pt 20.15pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">In September 2022, the IASB issued
amendments to IFRS 16 to clarify the requirements a seller-lessee uses to measure liabilities in a leaseback from a subsequent sale and
leaseback transaction to guarantee the seller-lessee does not recognize any amount of the gain or loss that relates to the right of use
it retains.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">These amendments have not had a significant
impact on the Group's financial statements.</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2024-01-01to2024-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001311" name="CEPU:IFRSIssuedButNotYetEffectivePolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_84A_ecustom--IFRSIssuedButNotYetEffectivePolicyTextBlock_zhyhUnz5AeQf" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><tr style="vertical-align: top">
<td style="width: 8.35pt"/><td style="width: 27.05pt">2.5.</td><td style="text-align: left; padding-right: 20.25pt"><span id="xdx_86F_zWqsHrWonNJ5">IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board
(IASB) issued but not yet effective</span></td></tr></table>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The following new and/or amended standards
and interpretations have been issued but were not effective as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements of
the Group. In this sense, only the new and/or amended standards and interpretations that the Group expects to be applicable in the future
are indicated. In general, the Group intends to adopt these standards, as applicable when they become effective.</p>
<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_239_z9Tejq8owDWf" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify"><br/>
<br/>
</p></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:exclude><p id="xdx_23A_zVH9hIVIKn5" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;&#160;</p></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Lack of interchangeability - Amendments
to IAS 21</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">In August 2023, the IASB issued amendments
to IAS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Currency Exchange Rates to clarify when entities should assess whether a currency is interchangeable
with another currency and when it is not, and how an entity determines the exchange rate to be applied when a currency is not interchangeable.
In addition, the amendments require information that allows users of their financial statements to assess how the lack of interchangeability
of a currency affects or is expected to affect its financial performance, financial position and cash flows.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The amendments will take effect for
annual periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025. Early application is allowed as long as this fact is disclosed. When applying the
modifications, the entities will not be able to re-express the comparative information.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">The amendments are not expected to have a
material impact on the Group's financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">IFRS 18 Presentation and disclosure
in the financial statements</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS
18, which replaces IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements. IFRS 18 introduces new requirements for the presentation of information
within the statement of income, including specific totals and subtotals. Additionally, entities must classify all income and expenses
within the statement of income into one of five categories: operating activities, investing activities, financing activities, income tax,
and discontinued operations, with the first three categories being new.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.25pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">It also requires entities to disclose
newly defined performance measures by management, subtotals of income and expenses, and includes new requirements to aggregate and disaggregate
financial information based on the &#8220;functions&#8221; identified from the primary financial statements and notes.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.4pt; text-align: justify">Limited scope amendments to IAS 7 Statement
of Cash Flows were issued, which include changing the starting point for determining cash flows generated by operations using the indirect
method, from &#8220;net profit or loss&#8221; to &#8220;operating profit or loss&#8221; and removing the optionality around the classification
of cash flows from dividends and interest. Consequently, new amendments to many other standards were made.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">IFRS 18 and the amendments to other
standards are effective for periods beginning on or after January 1, 2027; however, early application is allowed as long as this fact
is disclosed. IFRS 18 will be applied retrospectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">The Group is currently working to identify
all the effects that the amendments will have on the primary financial statements and notes to the financial statements.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public
Accountability: Disclosures</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued IFRS
19, which allows eligible entities to opt for reduced disclosure requirements while still applying the recognition, measurement, and presentation
requirements of other IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB). To be eligible, at the
end of the reporting period, the entity:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">(i) must be a subsidiary as defined
by IFRS 10, (ii) must not have public accountability, and (iii) must have a parent entity (either ultimate or intermediate) that prepares
consolidated financial statements that are available for public use and comply with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International
Accounting Standards Board (IASB).</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">IFRS 19 is effective for periods beginning
on or after January 1, 2027, with early application permitted.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 0 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A8_zIi10Vp8Sa7a" style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.25pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2024 CPSA holds
ownership interests of <span id="xdx_903_ecustom--OwnershipInterests_iI_pip0_dp_c20241231__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--InversoraDeGasDelCentroSAMember_zbrPZ7GpkuVi" title="Ownership Interests"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:OwnershipInterests" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_InversoraDeGasDelCentroSAMember" id="Fact001359" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">42.31</ix:nonFraction></span>% in Ecogas Inversiones S.A. ("Ecogas", formerly known as Inversora de Gas del Centro S.A., the
controlling company of Distribuidora de Gas del Centro S.A. &#8220;DGCE&#8221; and Distribuidora de Gas Cuyana S.A. &#8220;DGCU&#8221;),
and of <span id="xdx_905_ecustom--OwnershipInterests_iI_pip0_dp_c20241231__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DistribuidoraDeGasDelCentroSAMember_zfjnTTOjqXLj" title="Ownership Interests"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:OwnershipInterests" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_DistribuidoraDeGasDelCentroSAMember" id="Fact001361" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">17.20</ix:nonFraction></span>% in DGCE (from now on, &#8220;Grupo ECOGAS&#8221;). Consequently, the Group holds, both directly and indirectly, a <span id="xdx_90F_ecustom--OwnershipInterests_iI_pip0_dp_c20241231__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DGCEMember_z83hxVcJVlLd" title="Ownership Interests"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:OwnershipInterests" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_DGCEMember" id="Fact001363" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">40.59</ix:nonFraction></span>%
of the capital stock of DGCE, and, indirectly, a <span id="xdx_900_ecustom--OwnershipInterests_iI_pip0_dp_c20241231__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DGCUMember_zvBzMeNeDih1" title="Ownership Interests"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:OwnershipInterests" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_DGCUMember" id="Fact001365" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">21.58</ix:nonFraction></span>% interest in DGCU. The Company does not control such companies.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.2pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">Ecogas is a public entity listed on
BYMA. DGCE's main activity is the provision of the public service of distribution of natural gas by networks in the provinces of C&#243;rdoba,
La Rioja and Catamarca, while the main activity of DGCU is the provision of the public service of distribution of natural gas by networks
in the provinces of Mendoza, San Juan and San Luis.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.05pt 20.1pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">During May 2024, December 2023
and April 2022 the Group received dividends from the ECOGAS Group of <span id="xdx_905_eifrs-full--DividendsReceived_pn3n3_c20240501__20240531_zsrJ1MMyKAC5" title="Dividends received"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsReceived" contextRef="From2024-05-012024-05-31" id="Fact001367" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="ARS">2,289,114</ix:nonFraction></span>, <span id="xdx_902_eifrs-full--DividendsReceived_pn3n3_c20231201__20231231_zYySZmixFAbk" title="Dividends received"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsReceived" contextRef="From2023-12-012023-12-31" id="Fact001369" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="ARS">20,896,643</ix:nonFraction></span> and <span id="xdx_90A_eifrs-full--DividendsReceived_pn3n3_c20220401__20220430_zLVJgr49V1r3" title="Dividends received"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsReceived" contextRef="From2022-04-012022-04-30" id="Fact001371" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="ARS">665,614</ix:nonFraction></span>, respectively.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 11.45pt 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">On December 19, 2024, Ecogas
carried out a public offering of subscription of shares in kind and a voluntary exchange, which consisted of (i) a voluntary public exchange
offer of DGCU shares for new ordinary shares of Ecogas at an exchange ratio equivalent to 15.83467388 DGCU shares for each new share and
(ii) a voluntary public exchange offer of DGCE shares for new ordinary shares of Ecogas at an exchange ratio equivalent to 12.55431094
DGCE shares for each new share. The settlement date for the share exchange was January 17, 2025. As a result of the exchange offer, from
that date, CPSA&#180;s resulting direct participation in Ecogas is <span id="xdx_90B_ecustom--DirectParticipationPercentage_iI_pip0_dp_c20241219__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--EcogasMember_zIVVfh5m5zgc" title="Direct participation percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:DirectParticipationPercentage" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-19_custom_EcogasMember" id="Fact001373" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">26.17</ix:nonFraction></span>%, maintaining the <span id="xdx_90B_ecustom--DirectParticipationPercentage_iI_pip0_dp_c20241219__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DGCEMember_zJqF3u8s6iHi" title="Direct participation percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:DirectParticipationPercentage" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-19_custom_DGCEMember" id="Fact001375" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">17.20</ix:nonFraction></span>% direct participation in DGCE. Consequently,
as of the issuance date of these financial statements, the Group directly and indirectly owns <span id="xdx_902_ecustom--DirectAndIndirectOwnershipPercentage_iI_pip0_dp_c20241219__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DGCEMember_zyOmlhEw7RL5" title="Direct ownership percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:DirectAndIndirectOwnershipPercentage" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-19_custom_DGCEMember" id="Fact001377" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">38.56</ix:nonFraction></span>% of DGCE's share package and indirectly
owns <span id="xdx_90B_ecustom--IndirectOwnershipPercentage_iI_pip0_dp_c20241219__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--DGCEMember_zI16753GgNHd" title="Indirect ownership percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="CEPU:IndirectOwnershipPercentage" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-19_custom_DGCEMember" id="Fact001379" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">24.36</ix:nonFraction></span>% of DGCU's share package.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0.1pt 0 0; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 8.35pt; text-align: justify">On March 31, 2025, CPSA&#8217;s Board
of Directors approved proceeding with the corporate reorganization whereby, subject to approval by the Shareholders&#8217; Meeting of
the companies involved convened for May 22, 2025, CPSA will spin off its shares in Ecogas and <span id="xdx_90D_eifrs-full--Cash_iI_pn3n3_c20241231__ifrs-full--CounterpartiesAxis__custom--EcogasMember_zJw4jV0ZmaJ5" title="Cash"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:Cash" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_EcogasMember" id="Fact001381" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3" scale="3" unitRef="ARS">305,000</ix:nonFraction></span> in cash, to be absorbed by Ecogas
as of the effective date of the spin-off and merger. The effective date of the spin-off and merger shall occur after CNV grants administrative
approval. The shares that Ecogas issues in exchange for the incorporation of said spin-off assets will be received directly by the shareholders
of CPSA as a capital reimbursement, in accordance with the procedure that the Ecogas Board of Directors will inform the CPSA shareholders
in due course.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0 20.05pt 0 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>
